images.title: Both numbers fit inside
images.purpose: Recap the LCM method by showing the built LCM of 12 and 18 contains each number, so each divides it.
images.composition: One row of four prime tiles in the centre with a teal bracket above and an amber bracket below, and two short check lines underneath; plenty of white space.
exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 reddish purple #CC79A7 square tiles reading 2, 2, 3, 3 from left to right.
A teal #0072B2 bracket above the row spanning tiles 1, 2 and 3 (2, 2, 3), labelled 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 above it.
An amber #E69F00 bracket below the row spanning tiles 2, 3 and 4 (2, 3, 3), labelled 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 below it.
Result line under the amber label: LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36.
Two short check lines in green #009E73 under the result, side by side: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 and 36 ÷ 18 = 2.
rejection: other than exactly 4 tiles, or tiles not reading 2, 2, 3, 3
a bracket spanning the wrong tiles
any of the numbers 30, 72, 54, 105, 195, 65, 222 or 370 appearing
images.takeaway: The LCM holds every number's primes, so each number divides it exactly.
images.description: Prime tiles 2, 2, 3, 3 with a bracket over 2, 2, 3 for 12 and a bracket under 2, 3, 3 for 18, LCM = 36, checked by 36 ÷ 12 = 3 and 36 ÷ 18 = 2.
images.context: Shown beside the LCM builder practice tool.
images.teaching_notes: After building an LCM, find each number inside the tile row and do the division check.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap shows the check that each number divides the LCM.
